summary:
The Singapore Football League (SFL), affiliated with the Football Association of Singapore, is the country’s second and third football tiers. Its clubs can enter the Singapore FA Cup, but cannot be promoted to the professional Singapore Premier League (SPL), which has no promotion or relegation. SFL Division 2 clubs can move between the SFL and the fourth-tier Island Wide League.

The league began in 1975 as the National Football League (NFL), formed from a 118-team structure into three divisions with 30 clubs. Its Division One was Singapore’s top tier until the FAS Premier League replaced it in 1988. The professional S.League, now the SPL, began in 1996. The NFL was restructured in 2016–17 and renamed the SFL in 2020; the pandemic delayed its return until 2022.

The SFL has two divisions and is largely amateur, though some clubs are semi-professional. Singapore Khalsa Association won Division One from 2022 to 2024, before Singapore Cricket Club took the 2025 title. The 2026 season is scheduled to continue into 2027 to align with the SPL calendar.
